body.text: Your columnist woke up one morning in America to find the news outlets abuzz with the story of President Donald Trump evading an assassination attempt by hiding in an airline catering cart, back on July 8 when he departed the NATO summit in Turkey. Facts are stranger than fiction. So many attempts on the corrupt authoritarian‘s life, all unsuccessful. It is geopolitical slapstick.

America claims that Iran was planning to use an anti-aircraft missile against the President’s aircraft, known as Air Force One. American intelligence found that the Iranians had discovered the building where Trump was staying, and on which floor. It could be true—despite their profession of independence, the US legacy media which faithfully reported its government’s claims is no better than our Godi media—or it could be Israeli misinformation fed into the US national security system, something we’ve repeatedly seen even before this February’s war on Iran.

I’m as skeptical about it as about the assassination attempt while Trump was on the election trail in Butler, Pennsylvania, in 2024, when a bullet grazed his ear miraculously without damaging it in the least. “He took a bullet for you,” crazed the Make America Great Again (MAGA) followers shrieked throughout the rest of the campaign. Nonetheless, the Iranians reportedly tried to kill Trump several times after he ordered the assassination of General Qasem Soleimani at Baghdad‘s airport in January 2020; former President Joe Biden is said to have foiled one Iranian assassination attempt.

Though there were two Air Force One aircraft at Trump’s disposal in Turkey—the second was the retrofitted (at a cost of $1 billion) 747 gifted by Qatar—the secret service decided to use neither and put Trump in a C-130 transport aircraft to England, where he switched aircraft again. Some Americans compare hiding in the catering cart to a James Bond maneuver, while others admit “it doesn’t make him look too good”, which is an understatement. Memes have popped up showing Trump comically stuffed into an airplane meal trolley; they are as hilarious as the “Chappan-inch“ videos of Prime Minister Narendra Modi clapping and dancing.
The news leaked a month after the incident, which means it is a deliberate leak. This subterfuge can’t be used again, but more importantly, it makes one wonder why Trump green-lit the leak.

Perhaps it is because his polls are plummeting. Every Tuesday there is a primary election where all the excitement surrounds Democratic Party candidates, not the Republicans, giving us an indication of which way the November mid-term polls are heading. The Democratic Socialists are still on a roll, with only Francesca Hong as a surprise loser in the primary for Wisconsin Governor. Trump has already blamed his party for whatever happens in the mid-terms, absolving himself in advance. Assassination attempts always garner a few sympathy votes.

Or maybe the leak was provoked by Iran’s declaration this week, that it would not further negotiate with America to end the war until Trump left office. Normally, that would be on January 20, 2029, though Trump is said to be intent of further institutional capture and prolonging his reign. Iran also demanded $300 billion in compensation, the release of $100 billion in frozen assets, and the withdrawal of US forces from the region. The Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

In America, it is openly declared by military experts and commentators across the spectrum that this is their nation’s greatest ever strategic defeat, and all because of Trump. A war that was supposed to end in days has entered its sixth month and has turned Iran into a geopolitical major power.

Experts wonder how the US’ missile stockpile depleted, while Iran‘s is refreshed. Was it because of arms exports to Ukraine? But so many said that America dumped old munitions on the Ukrainians. Is the depletion because of a waste of missiles to sink boats off the coast of South America? The missile shortfall is probably the most tangible example of imperial overstretch.

Iran is sitting pretty, almost taunting the US to launch a ground invasion. That would be the end of Trump, and it would also be another chapter in the further fragmentation of America, an already polarised nation.

Perhaps Trump thought it necessary to further demonise the Iranian regime, and hence the leak of his furtive escape from Turkey, unharmed, in the company of fried chicken and hamburgers. After all, his MAGA followers take as gospel Trump’s assertion that the Iranian regime killed 52,000 citizens in last December’s uprising against the massive currency depreciation (that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent claimed was engineered by him). Only 3,000 Iranians died in those protests (which is still a lot, though many were killed by Israel’s Mossad to provoke further protest), but Trump has continuously inflated those figures to 10,000 and then to 30,000 before the latest count. Secretary of State Marco Rubio repeatedly splutters about the “evil terrorist” regime in Teheran, while it is his country that kills infant schoolgirls.

Demonising the Iranians as would-be assassins does not make sense if the war is going to end soon. Trump is a well-known narcissist who will not stomach a loss. (He continues to whine about the 2020 election having been stolen from him, though there has been no evidence supporting his claims, and his legal challenges have all been thrown out of various courts.) Indeed, Trump made counter-demands of Iran this week as compensation for its “regional victims”.

We can safely assume the war will continue for years; the Iranians have said so, and Trump refuses to budge. In the meantime, we will see many propaganda missives fly, like assassination attempts on both sides; a ship will occasionally be bombed, to remind us that a war is going on; and oil prices will remain high. The only consolation we have is a picture of Trump cowering inside a meal trolley, unable any longer to shoulder what Rudyard Kipling called “the white man’s burden”.
Aditya Sinha is a writer living on the outskirts of Delhi.
